summary: Bidirectional automation can create feedback loops, propagate false mappings, and flood owners with low-value updates. The write-back path also expands the companion from a read interface into a privileged change system.

points.text: A generated companion edit can trigger a source change, which triggers regeneration and another semantically equivalent edit; without convergence rules, the system oscillates or churns commits.
Probabilistic trace links and entity matching can update the wrong requirement, component, or decision. Once written back, the false link appears authoritative and influences later reconciliation.
If every detected mismatch becomes a pull request or approval task, reviewers face a permanent queue and start bulk-accepting cosmetic synchronization.
A companion that can propose or apply source changes needs stronger identity, authorization, injection defenses, and audit controls than a generated read-only site.
